text:
simon (Finance): FYI vendor NordicCompute sent INV-3421 for ,900 NOK. Invoice shows supplier VAT: NO999888777, but billing party is listed as NordicCompute AB (SE). They added a 'withholding protection / gross-up' clause for Norwegian WHT on services. Can we pay?
leah (AP): Wait, mixed country entity. Do we have a PO?
simon (Finance): PO 47002, matching amount. Uploaded PDF: https://drive.redwood/nordiccompute/INV-3421.pdf
purchasing-bot: PO 47002: approved for payment, but blocked by tax evidence flag.
oleks (Tax): Quick checks: NO VAT suggests Norway registration. If the invoicing entity is Swedish (AB) but they claim a Norwegian VAT number, that's inconsistent. We need entity-level proof. Also, Norway sometimes withholds on cross-border service royalties/payments depending on nature of services and treaty. Vendor asking for gross-up is not standard.
nidhi (Legal): Agree. Gross-up shifts withholding risk to us; we generally refuse unless commercial negotiation. Ask them to confirm which legal entity is billing and provide either: 1) Norwegian VAT reg certificate matching NO999888777, or 2) Swedish org number and Swedish VAT (if billing from AB), or 3) certificate of tax residency (TRC) if they want treaty relief.
simon (Finance): On invoice they listed "NordicCompute AB (branch in NO)" as free text.
leah (AP): Action for simon: request reissued invoice that matches legal entity + tax id, and remove gross-up clause. Also request TRC if they claim treaty withholding relief. We should not gross-up here.
oleks (Tax): If they are Norwegian-registered and services are supplied in Norway, standard Norwegian VAT (MVA) may apply, but for cross-border B2B services reverse-charge could apply. We need clear place-of-supply info and their VAT residency. If withholding applies (rare for services), we need vendor bank-level indemnity or a signed statement.
simon (Finance): Sent vendor note: "Please reissue invoice matching the legal billing entity and tax registration. Remove the gross-up clause. If you claim treaty relief from Norwegian WHT, attach a TRC. Otherwise we will pay net and will not accept gross-up."
vendor (NordicCompute) (via email, pasted): "We will provide TRC and reissue from the Swedish parent to avoid Norway VAT. The gross-up was inserted by our sales ops to cover any local WHT. We'll remove it."
nidhi (Legal): Good. If they reissue from SE parent and attach confirmation, we can pay. If they insist on gross-up later, escalate to procurement and legal for commercial sign-off.
leah (AP): Marking invoice on hold. I'll unlock for payment once we get either: reissued invoice + matching PO or TRC proving no WHT.
simon (Finance): Noted. I'll follow up in 24h. Thanks. :white_check_mark:
